set.explanation: Penicillins and cephalosporins commonly cause morbilliform (maculopapular) drug eruptions.
Recent amoxicillin raises beta-lactamase–producing organism risk in sinusitis.
Clindamycin has high C. difficile risk.
Azithromycin can prolong QT → torsades de pointes.
Acute bronchitis in a healthy adult: supportive care (rest, fluids); antibiotics are not indicated.
Screening tests (rule out disease) should have high sensitivity.
Typical bacterial CAP often shows lobar infiltrates on chest imaging.
Healthy outpatient CAP without comorbidities: macrolide such as azithromycin is first-line.
PCN allergy (hives): azithromycin is an appropriate respiratory fluoroquinolone/macrolide alternative.
Anemia = reduction in at least one RBC measure (Hgb, Hct, or RBC count).
